findings.passage: We knew from the beginning that Texas' voter id law was meant to disenfranchise voters. The ruling will help the grandmother who no longer has her driver's license exercise her right to vote. It will allow the college student, who was barred from using a student id to vote, access to their polling place.
findings.note: Press release issued in his name after a federal appeals court struck down the Texas photo ID law; he describes the ID law's effect on people without a driver's license and on students whose student ID was not accepted.

findings.passage: Instead, we must focus on making voting more accessible for our fellow Texans by implementing policies such as universal vote by mail, countywide polling, 24-hour and drive-thru voting options, expanding voter identifications and providing necessary resources for our election officials.
findings.note: Written statement entered in the Senate Journal on the SB 1 conference report; it opposes the bill and lists policies he prefers, including expanding voter identifications.

findings.passage: This bill is a solution in search of a non-existent problem. The Texas Secretary of State, our top election official, stated that the 2020 elections were safe and secure.
findings.note: Same Senate Journal statement on SB 1; he says the bill addresses no real problem and cites the Secretary of State on the 2020 elections.

SB 116 (2023), by him and another senator, caption 'Relating to requiring a voter to present proof of identification'; his 2022-11-14 bill-filing release titles it 'Expanded Voter Identification'. Last action 02/15/2023 referred to State Affairs.

findings.passage: First, we need to restrict access to weapons of war that have been designed for use by trained soldiers.
findings.note: Official Senate press release after the Santa Fe school shooting; he calls for limiting access to military-style weapons.

findings.passage: Second, we must review existing laws closing all of the loopholes requiring that every sale of a firearm need to undergo a background check and then create new laws that promote Common Sense gun safety.
findings.note: Same release; he calls for a background check on every firearm sale and new gun safety laws.

findings.passage: The tragic reality is that mass shootings have become commonplace and law enforcement lacks the proper tools to keep guns out of the hands of dangerous or unstable people.
findings.note: Official press release after a clinic shooting in Colorado; his statement continues that lawmakers at federal and state levels should pass thoughtful, commonsense laws to end mass shootings.

findings.passage: We want to do universal background checks.
findings.note: Quoted by KSAT (copy hosted on a congressional member site) after a San Antonio town hall following the El Paso and Odessa shootings.

findings.passage: We want to do red flag laws that make us safer.
findings.note: Same KSAT story as quoted; he supports red-flag laws.
